title: Car lights shader construction
summary: Recovered 0x576f00..0x577039 as a genuine thiscall member returning this. Initializes a 0xa4-byte shader object through the accepted base helper, copies the unchecked variant and four manager resources, installs the original vtable identity, creates a 4x4 identity transform, performs ordered matWorldViewProj and lightColour lookups, and invokes accepted common-parameter initialization. Original callers select variants 0 through 3. Dependencies are explicit port bindings; no shader helper internals are reconstructed here.
test_description: 96 direct original-versus-source cases: variants 0,1,2,3,0x7fffffff,0x80000000,0xffffffff,0xdeadbeef; two initial object fills; distinct and aliased parameter resources; zero-count, descriptor-failure, and three-null-index common-lookup outcomes. Compares returned this, complete object and surrounding canaries, ordered resource callback arguments/results, identity transform, unchanged manager/resources/cookies, and explicit initialized test-owned FS head restoration after every invocation. Uses exact-size .manager/.cookie/.cookie_guard fixtures and correct thiscall/stdcall declarations. Local GCC i386 differential executable passes; all four accepted reference sections independently compared byte-for-byte with immutable Game.exe.
known_limits: Normal completion only: Windows exception dispatch, base cleanup during unwind, and compiler SEH cookie infrastructure are not implemented by portable source.
Common/base/parameter helpers remain accepted original dependencies supplied by test-only member bindings; a Linux port must provide their recovered implementations separately.

Controlled resource callbacks validate constructor interactions, not D3DX or rendering internals. Common lookup tests cover failure, empty descriptors and null indexed handles; successful common name matching is outside this fixture.
Requires valid manager and both parameter objects, as does original. Invalid pointers and aliasing the object with manager storage are not supported port contracts or tested cases.
Original vtable identity is retained as a 32-bit field; this is an x86 layout reconstruction, not a complete host virtual-dispatch implementation. No byte-matching source claim.
Pinned MSVC helper is absent in this sandbox. GCC C++11 compatibility compile passes; native MSVC2013 compilation remains for the trusted coordinator.
